description_good_justification: The project provides a clear description in README.md: 'Passwordless TYPO3 backend authentication via Passkeys (WebAuthn/FIDO2)' with comprehensive overview, features, and API documentation. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be#overview

contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to contribute, including development setup, quality requirements, and PR process. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents quality requirements (PHPStan level 10, PER-CS3.0 code style, unit tests, mutation tests) and PR process including conventional commits and signed commits. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

floss_license_osi_justification: GPL-2.0-or-later is approved by the Open Source Initiative. See https://opensource.org/licenses/GPL-2.0 and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/LICENSE

english_justification: All project documentation, code comments, README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, and issue templates are in English. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained with recent releases (v0.5.0 February 2026), regular commits, responsive issue handling, and comprehensive CI/CD pipeline. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/releases

repo_distributed_justification: The project uses Git, a distributed version control system, hosted on GitHub. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique semantic version (0.1.0 through 0.5.0), with signed Git tags and corresponding GitHub releases. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/releases
version_semver_justification: The project uses semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) for all releases. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/releases
version_tags_justification: All releases are tagged in Git with signed tags (git tag -s). Tags: 0.1.0 through 0.5.0. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/tags
release_notes_justification: Each release has detailed release notes in the Changelog documentation and on GitHub Releases. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Documentation/Changelog/Index.rst and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/releases

report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is used as the public issue tracker, with structured templates for bugs and feature requests. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/issues
report_responses_justification: The project is actively maintained with recent commits within the last 90 days and responsive issue handling. SECURITY.md commits to response timelines (48 hours for critical, 5 business days for high). See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/SECURITY.md#response-timeline
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a permanent, searchable archive of all reported bugs. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are tracked via GitHub Issues with a dedicated feature request template. The project actively responds to and implements requested enhancements. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the vulnerability reporting process: use GitHub Security Advisories for private reporting, includes what to include in reports and response timeline by severity. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Vulnerabilities are reported privately via GitHub Security Advisories. SECURITY.md explicitly states 'Do NOT open a public GitHub issue for security vulnerabilities.' See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/security/advisories and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md defines response SLAs: Critical 48 hours initial response / 7 days fix, High 5 business days / 30 days, Medium 10 business days / 90 days. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/SECURITY.md#response-timeline
build_justification: The project uses Composer for PHP dependency management and npm for JavaScript. Build commands documented in README.md and composer.json scripts section. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/composer.json
build_common_tools_justification: The project uses Composer (PHP standard build tool), PHPUnit (testing), PHPStan (static analysis), PHP-CS-Fixer (code style), and npm/Vitest (JavaScript). All are widely-used FLOSS tools. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/composer.json
build_floss_tools_justification: All build tools are FLOSS: Composer (MIT), PHPUnit (BSD-3-Clause), PHPStan (MIT), PHP-CS-Fixer (MIT), Infection (BSD-3-Clause), Vitest (MIT). See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/composer.json
test_justification: The project has a comprehensive test suite: 301 unit tests, fuzz tests (3 suites), 24 functional tests, and JavaScript tests. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/tree/main/Tests
test_invocation_justification: Tests are easily invoked via standard Composer scripts: 'composer ci:test:php:unit', 'composer ci:test:php:functional', 'composer ci:test:php:fuzz', 'npm run test:js'. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/composer.json
test_most_justification: The test suite covers unit, fuzz, functional, and mutation testing across all major code paths. Mutation testing (Infection) enforces MSI >= 80% and covered MSI >= 80%, ensuring most branches are tested. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Build/infection.json5
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions CI runs on every push to main and every PR. The CI matrix tests across PHP 8.2-8.5 and TYPO3 12/13/14 with lint, PHPStan, unit, functional, fuzz, and mutation jobs. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states: 'New features must include unit tests' and 'Bug fixes should include a regression test'. PR template includes checkbox 'I have added tests covering my changes'. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#writing-tests
tests_are_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests for all contributions, enforced by the PR checklist and CI quality gates including mutation testing. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#writing-tests and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests for all new features and bug fixes. Tests are documented with PHPDoc comments and organized in structured directories (Unit, Functional, Fuzz). See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#writing-tests
warnings_justification: PHPStan level 10 (maximum strictness) with ergebnis/phpstan-rules is enforced in CI. PHP strict_types=1 is declared in all 23 PHP source files. PHP-CS-Fixer enforces strict_param rule. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Build/phpstan.neon and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Build/.php-cs-fixer.php
warnings_fixed_justification: All warnings from PHPStan level 10, PHP-CS-Fixer, and CodeQL are fixed before merge. CI pipeline fails on any warning or error. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
warnings_strict_justification: PHPStan runs at maximum level 10 with strict rules (ergebnis/phpstan-rules). PHP strict_types=1 in all source files. PHP-CS-Fixer enforces PER-CS3.0 with strict_param. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Build/phpstan.neon
know_secure_design_justification: The Security documentation chapter demonstrates knowledge of secure design principles: HMAC-signed challenge tokens, nonce replay protection, rate limiting, user enumeration prevention, credential ownership verification, and signature counter validation. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Documentation/Security/Index.rst
know_common_errors_justification: The extension addresses common security errors: timing attacks (hash_equals), replay attacks (nonce protection), XSS (label sanitization), CSRF (TYPO3 backend tokens), user enumeration (randomized timing), injection (parameterized queries via TYPO3 ConnectionPool). See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Documentation/Security/Index.rst
crypto_published_justification: All cryptographic mechanisms are fully documented: HMAC-SHA256 for challenge tokens, random_bytes for challenge/nonce generation, hash_equals for constant-time comparison. No custom cryptographic algorithms are used. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Documentation/Security/Index.rst#hmac-signed-challenge-tokens
crypto_call_justification: The extension uses well-established cryptographic primitives from PHP's standard library (hash_hmac, random_bytes, hash_equals, bin2hex) and delegates WebAuthn verification to the web-auth/webauthn-lib library. No custom crypto implementations. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Classes/Service/ChallengeService.php
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptographic functionality uses FLOSS implementations: PHP's built-in OpenSSL functions and the web-auth/webauthn-lib v5.2 library (MIT license). See https://github.com/web-auth/webauthn-lib and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/composer.json
crypto_keylength_justification: The extension enforces minimum 32-character TYPO3 encryption key for HMAC-SHA256 signing, uses 32-byte (256-bit) random challenges, and supports ES256/ES384/ES512/RS256 signing algorithms for WebAuthn. Key lengths meet NIST recommendations. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Documentation/Security/Index.rst#hmac-signed-challenge-tokens
crypto_working_justification: The default cryptographic algorithms (HMAC-SHA256 for challenge tokens, ES256 for WebAuthn) are industry-standard and considered secure by NIST. No deprecated algorithms are used. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Classes/Service/ChallengeService.php
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The extension does not use known-weak algorithms. HMAC-SHA256 is used for token signing. WebAuthn uses ECDSA/RSA. Constant-time comparison (hash_equals) prevents timing attacks. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Documentation/Security/Index.rst
crypto_pfs_justification: This is a TYPO3 extension that does not implement TLS/network protocols. Perfect forward secrecy is the responsibility of the web server and TYPO3 infrastructure. The extension requires HTTPS (documented in Installation guide). See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Documentation/Installation/Index.rst
crypto_password_storage_justification: This extension replaces password authentication with WebAuthn passkeys. It does not store passwords. Password handling is delegated to TYPO3 core's SaltedPasswordService. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be#overview
crypto_random_justification: The extension uses PHP's random_bytes() (CSPRNG) for all random data: 32-byte challenges and 16-byte nonces. random_int() is used for timing randomization. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Classes/Service/ChallengeService.php
delivery_mitm_justification: The extension is distributed via Composer (Packagist over HTTPS) and the TYPO3 Extension Repository (TER over HTTPS). GitHub releases use signed tags (git tag -s). See https://packagist.org/packages/netresearch/nr-passkeys-be and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/ter-publish.yml
delivery_unsigned_justification: Release tags are signed locally with GPG (git tag -s) before pushing. Composer verifies package integrity via checksums in composer.lock. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/tags
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to fixing critical vulnerabilities within 7 days, high within 30 days, and medium within 90 days. All timelines are within or equal to the 60-day expectation for critical/high issues. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/SECURITY.md#response-timeline
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: SECURITY.md commits to fixing critical vulnerabilities within 7 days. No known unpatched critical vulnerabilities exist. Dependency vulnerabilities are monitored via Dependabot, composer audit in CI, and dependency-review action. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/SECURITY.md#response-timeline
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository contains no credentials or secrets. .gitignore excludes build artifacts. CI secrets are stored in GitHub encrypted secrets. The TYPO3 encryption key is read from server configuration, never committed. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.gitignore
hardened_site_justification: The project site (GitHub) uses HTTPS, two-factor authentication, branch protection rules (signed commits, required reviews, required CI checks, no force pushes). GitHub Actions use SHA-pinned dependencies and step-security/harden-runner on every job. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/SECURITY.md#branch-protection and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
static_analysis_justification: PHPStan level 10 (maximum) with ergebnis/phpstan-rules runs in CI. PHP-CS-Fixer enforces PER-CS3.0 coding standard. CodeQL analyzes JavaScript/TypeScript and GitHub Actions. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL (SAST) analyzes for common vulnerability patterns in JavaScript and Actions. PHPStan level 10 catches type errors, null references, and dead code. dependency-review-action blocks high-severity vulnerable dependencies. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: PHPStan level 10 with 0 errors enforced in CI (pipeline fails on any issue). PHP-CS-Fixer enforced in CI (fails on style violations). All static analysis findings are fixed before merge. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis (PHPStan, PHP-CS-Fixer, CodeQL) runs on every push to main and every pull request. Additionally, PHPStan and linting run as pre-commit hooks via CaptainHook. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Build/captainhook.json
dynamic_analysis_justification: The project uses fuzz testing (3 fuzz test suites for challenge tokens, credential IDs, and request payloads) and mutation testing (Infection MSI >= 80%) as forms of dynamic analysis. Functional tests with MySQL exercise real database interactions. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/tree/main/Tests/Fuzz and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Fuzz tests specifically target security-sensitive code paths: challenge token parsing (ChallengeTokenFuzzTest), credential ID handling (CredentialIdFuzzTest), and request payload parsing (RequestPayloadFuzzTest). These detect memory safety and input validation issues. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/tree/main/Tests/Fuzz
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: PHP assertions are used in production code for type safety (assert for LanguageService and LoggerInterface types). PHP's strict_types=1 is enabled in all 23 source files, providing runtime type checking. PHPUnit runs with assertions enabled. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Classes/Authentication/PasskeyAuthenticationService.php and https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/Classes/UserSettings/PasskeySettingsPanel.php
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: All dynamic analysis issues are fixed: fuzz tests, functional tests, and mutation tests must pass in CI before merge. Mutation testing enforces MSI >= 80% ensuring surviving mutants are addressed. See https://github.com/netresearch/t3x-nr-passkeys-be/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
